title.value: Metadata Archaeology: Unearthing Data Subsets by Leveraging Training Dynamics
title.justification: The title reflects the primary focus of the paper, which is on uncovering hidden data subsets and metadata through analyzing training dynamics.
title.quote: Metadata Archaeology: Unearthing Data Subsets by Leveraging Training Dynamics

extractions.description: This paper introduces a framework called Metadata Archaeology, specifically Metadata Archaeology via Probe Dynamics (MAP-D), which focuses on efficiently uncovering and inferring metadata within datasets. The methodology involves curating data subsets and leveraging training dynamics to identify mislabeled, atypical, or minority-group examples, among others, without relying heavily on prior domain knowledge or human annotations. It aims to address data quality and diversity issues in machine learning by providing a unified approach instead of tackling individual metadata issues in isolation.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central focus of the paper is on improving machine learning data quality and dynamics, rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development challenges. There is no specific mention of sustainability issues in the context of climate or ecology within the text.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Even in these datasets, and typically in ‘untidy’ or raw data, practitioners are faced with significant issues of data quality and diversity which can be prohibitively labor intensive to address.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily deals with methodologies to improve the efficiency of data subset identification and does not address any specific sustainable development categories related to climate or ecology.
primary_category.quote: Our work is orthogonal to these methods: we instead focus on providing a unified and efficient framework for Metadata Archaeology – uncovering and inferring metadata of examples in a dataset.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes in the paper that align with any specific climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: We use the term Metadata Archaeology to describe the problem of inferring metadata across a more complete data taxonomy.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not delve into any sub-categories related to sustainable development as its focus is on machine learning datasets and metadata.
primary_sub_category.quote: We curate different subsets of data that might exist in a dataset (e.g. mislabeled, atypical, or out-of-distribution examples) using simple transformations, and leverage differences in learning dynamics between these probe suites to infer metadata of interest.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As there are no secondary climate or ecological themes, no applicable sub-categories can be identified.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The underlying issue with such approaches is the assumption of a single, known type of data issue.

applications.value: Auditing datasets and debugging model training
applications.justification: One application of the MAP-D framework is using it to audit large-scale datasets or debug model training, which could be relevant in sustainability if applied to datasets pertaining to ecological or climate data.
applications.quote: We show how MAP-D could be leveraged to audit large-scale datasets or debug model training, with negligible added cost.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's focus is specifically on improving machine learning processes through better data subset identification and metadata inference, which does not fall under existing climate/ecological categories.
new_primary_category.quote: Our approach, which we term Metadata Archaeology via Probe Dynamics (MAP-D), leverages distinct differences in training dynamics for different curated subsets to enable specialized treatment and effective labelling of different metadata categories.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The introduced methodology ('Metadata Archaeology') does not readily fit into any existing sub-category focused on sustainable development, aligning more with general machine learning practices.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we are interested in moving away from a siloed treatment of different data properties. We use the term Metadata Archaeology to describe the problem of inferring metadata across a more complete data taxonomy.
